name: United States Military Academy

athletics.revShareNotes: Federal service academy: cadet-athletes are federal personnel, so direct House-settlement revenue sharing does not map cleanly. Opt-in status not verified.
athletics.note: Not in the USA Today public-school finance database (federal academy; athletics run through the Army West Point Athletic Association).

ratingNotes: FB: 2024 12-2, won the American title in its first season (beat Tulane in the title game) plus an Independence Bowl win. Option-based Monken program; fell back in 2025 (exact record not verified). MBB: Patriot League; has never made the NCAA tournament. WBB: Patriot contender (NCAA 2006, 2014). Olympic: 30-plus-sport academy program, typically Directors' Cup ~#70-100. Brand: Army-Navy on CBS and service-academy recognition far above a typical G6 school. Political: federal (DoD, Congress/NDAA, presidents attend Army-Navy), not a state.

president.name: Lt. Gen. Steven W. Gilland
president.title: Superintendent
president.note: Superintendent rotation as of Nov 2026 not verified

notes: Football-only member of the American since 2024; all other sports in the Patriot League. Since 2024 Army-Navy counts as an American conference game, so the two can meet a week after the American title game. That makes for a scheduling and tiebreak quirk the commissioner has to manage. Army-Navy itself stays a CBS property outside the American's ESPN deal. Earlier history: C-USA football 1998-2004, then FBS independent 2005-23. Federal levers: Secretary of Defense directives on academy athletics, Congress, and the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy (with Navy and Air Force). Federal service academy: control is set to 'public' but it is federally funded and has no state legislature.

name: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in, like the rest of the American's members. Pays well below the $20.5M cap; exact amount not verified.
athletics.note: Revenue/expense figures are approximate magnitudes from memory of the USA Today/Knight-Newhouse data, not verified this session.

ratingNotes: FB: program began 2013, reached FBS and C-USA in 2015, and has one bowl (2019 Bahamas). Biff Poggi was fired mid-2024. Tim Albin's 2025 debut season was poor (record not verified). MBB: 1977 Final Four as UNC Charlotte, last NCAA trip 2011, 2023 CBI champs. Fan base: top-25 TV market but thin engagement and a small stadium.

headFootballCoach.name: Tim Albin
headFootballCoach.note: Hired Dec 2024 from Ohio; status after 2026 season not verified

notes: Moved from C-USA to the American in 2023 (one of six C-USA schools taken). Its main asset is the Charlotte market, a top-25 DMA that also hosts ACC events and the Duke's Mayo Bowl, which makes it an expansion piece for any league chasing markets. Governed by the UNC System Board of Governors, so North Carolina legislative politics (ECU/ACC dynamics) can reach it.

name: East Carolina University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; partial-cap payments typical of the American. Amount not verified.
athletics.note: Approximate finances, not verified this session.

ratingNotes: FB: Blake Harrell took over as interim in Oct 2024 and was made permanent, then won the 2024 Military Bowl over NC State. Bowl-caliber in 2025 (record not verified). MBB: no NCAA trip since 1993. WBB: 2023 American tournament champs. Olympic: baseball is a national-level program (Clark-LeClair). Fan base is among the best in the G6 for attendance and travel.
notes: Has wanted into the ACC for decades and has allies in the North Carolina General Assembly, who have periodically pressed the UNC System and ACC schools to schedule or include ECU. If the ACC ever loses members, ECU is the obvious political pressure point. Large, loyal fan base in a small DMA. In-state ties with NC State and UNC carry statehouse leverage.

name: Florida Atlantic University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; partial-cap payments. Amount not verified.
athletics.note: Approximate finances; stadium naming-rights branding may differ.

ratingNotes: FB: peaked under Lane Kiffin with C-USA titles in 2017 and 2019. Zach Kittley (former Texas Tech OC) has been rebuilding since 2025. MBB: 2023 Final Four and 2024 NCAA under Dusty May, who left for Michigan in 2024. John Jakus (from Baylor) since 2025; the program has drifted toward the mid-pack since. Tiny arena.
notes: Its president is a former Republican state legislator, part of the politicized Florida Board of Governors presidential picks. Expect state political pressure on any realignment decision. The Boca Raton donor base is wealthy but has not mobilized for athletics at P4 scale. The 2023 Final Four is the brand peak and a hook for a basketball-first pitch. Plays FIU annually in the Shula Bowl.

name: University of Memphis

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in. Among the most aggressive G6 spenders: it signaled near-P4 player-compensation levels backed by local corporate and booster money. Exact amount not verified.
athletics.note: Approximate finances. Stadium is mid-renovation (multi-phase, publicly funded), so capacity is in flux.

ratingNotes: FB: went 11-2 with a Frisco Bowl win in 2024 and started 2025 hot. Ryan Silverfield left for Arkansas after 2025 (from memory, not verified). MBB: the G6's top hoops brand, with Final Fours in 1973 and 1985 (vacated) and 2008 (vacated). Won the 2025 American regular season and tournament and was an NCAA 5-seed. Penny Hardaway since 2018. Plays in an NBA arena.

headFootballCoach.name: Charles Huff
headFootballCoach.note: From memory: hired Dec 2025 from Southern Miss after Silverfield left for Arkansas. Not verified this session.

notes: The G6's loudest P4 aspirant. In July 2025 it pitched the Big 12 on a record entry package reported at over $200M, forgoing distributions for the back end of the Big 12 TV deal and accepting a performance-based removal clause. The Big 12 board rebuffed it; adding a member needs 12 of 16 votes. Memphis also explored moving basketball to the Big East. Donor and corporate base: FedEx (founder Fred Smith died in 2025), AutoZone and local billionaires. Tennessee state money is funding the Liberty Bowl stadium and FedExForum renovations, and state politicians lobby for P4 inclusion. High-probability actor in any realignment event.

name: United States Naval Academy

athletics.revShareNotes: Federal service academy: midshipmen are federal personnel. Opt-in status not verified.
athletics.note: Athletics run by the Naval Academy Athletic Association; not in the public-school finance databases.

ratingNotes: FB: 2024 10-3 with an Armed Forces Bowl win over Oklahoma. Consistent bowl team under Brian Newberry; strong 2025 (record not verified). MBB: Patriot League; no NCAA trip since 1998 (David Robinson era peak 1986-87). Olympic: large program, usually inside the Directors' Cup top ~75. Brand: Army-Navy and Notre Dame series give it national TV draw.

president.name: Lt. Gen. Michael J. Borgschulte (USMC)
president.title: Superintendent
president.note: From memory: named in 2025 after Vice Adm. Yvette Davids was removed by the Secretary of Defense. Not verified.

ad.name: Chet Gladchuk
ad.note: Long-tenured; retirement status as of 2026 not verified

notes: Football-only member of the American since 2015, when it joined as Big East football became the American; all other sports in the Patriot League. Its deal protects Army-Navy (CBS, conference game since 2024) and the Notre Dame series. FBS independent for over a century before 2015. Federal levers: DoD leadership turnover at the academies (2025), Congress and the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy. Federal service academy: control is set to 'public'.

name: University of North Texas

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; partial-cap payments. Amount not verified.

ratingNotes: FB: breakout 2025 under Eric Morris: 11-1 regular season, then lost the American title game to Tulane. Morris left for Oklahoma State (from memory). MBB: 2023 NIT champion. Coaches keep leaving for P4 jobs (Grant McCasland to Texas Tech in 2023, Ross Hodge to West Virginia in 2025). Daniyal Robinson since 2025.

headFootballCoach.name: Neal Brown
headFootballCoach.note: From memory: hired Dec 2025 after Eric Morris left for Oklahoma State. Not verified this session.

notes: R1 university with 47k students in the fast-growing DFW market (#4-5 DMA) and vocal Big 12-style ambitions. Moved C-USA to the American in 2023. It is a farm system for P4 coaches, the classic G6 talent-drain storyline. Under the UNT System and the Texas Legislature, which in Texas means real political leverage over conference moves.

name: William Marsh Rice University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in. Private school, so the payment level is not public; believed partial cap.
athletics.note: Private school, not in the USA Today database. EADA figures not retrieved this session.

ratingNotes: FB: 2023 bowl was its first since 2014. Scott Abell (from Davidson) has run an option offense since 2025. MBB: no NCAA trip since 1970. WBB: 2024 American tournament champs (NCAA). Olympic: baseball won the 2003 CWS. Academic brand is elite; athletic brand modest.
notes: Elite private AAU university in the #7 Houston DMA. A Southwest Conference orphan (1996) that P4 leagues have passed over in every expansion (Big 12 picked Houston in 2023). Its pitch is academics plus market. Low state political pressure. Rice Stadium (1950) hosted Super Bowl VIII and JFK's 1962 'moon speech'. Bayou Bucket rivalry with Houston.

name: University of South Florida

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; among the higher G6 payers. Amount not verified.
athletics.note: Approximate finances. An on-campus stadium (~35,000 seats, ~$340M) is under construction and targeted for 2027; Raymond James (Buccaneers) is the current home.

ratingNotes: FB: Alex Golesh rebuilt the program from 2023-25. 2025 opened with wins over Boise State and Florida (about 9-3). Golesh left for Auburn. Big East-era peak was a #2 ranking in 2007. MBB: won the 2024 American regular season under Amir Abdur-Rahim, who died in Oct 2024. Bryan Hodgson since 2025. WBB: Jose Fernandez, frequent NCAA team.

president.name: Moez Limayem
president.title: President
president.note: From memory: selected 2025 to succeed Rhea Law

headFootballCoach.name: Brian Hartline
headFootballCoach.note: From memory: Ohio State OC hired Dec 2025 after Golesh left for Auburn. Not verified this session.

notes: Passed over by the Big 12 in 2011, 2016 and 2021, while rival UCF got in for 2023. That still stings and drives the push for an on-campus stadium (target opening 2027), the centerpiece of its P4 case. AAU member since 2023. Large Tampa Bay market. Subject to the Florida Board of Governors and state politics (politicized presidential searches), so state pressure is high.

name: Temple University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; partial-cap payments. Amount not verified.
athletics.note: Approximate finances. Football rents the Philadelphia Eagles' stadium.

ratingNotes: FB: peaked in 2015-16 (2016 American title under Matt Rhule) and has slumped since. K.C. Keeler (FCS title winner at Delaware and Sam Houston) hired Dec 2024. MBB: historic program (John Chaney); last NCAA trip 2019. Fan base: tiny crowds in an NFL stadium.
notes: The Big East expelled Temple football (effective after 2004). It was readmitted for 2012-13 and carried over into the American. Its core value is the Philadelphia market, a top-5 DMA. The Lincoln Financial Field lease is costly, and community opposition killed an on-campus stadium plan around 2018. State-related university (Pennsylvania appropriation), so moderate statehouse pressure. Big 5 basketball city rivalries.

name: Tulane University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in. Private school, payment level not public; believed among the higher G6 payers.

arena.name: Avron B. Fogelman Arena in Devlin Fieldhouse

athletics.note: Private school, not in the USA Today database.

ratingNotes: FB: beat USC in the Cotton Bowl to finish 12-2 in 2022, lost the 2024 American title game to Army, won the 2025 American title over North Texas and made the 12-team CFP (lost at Ole Miss in the first round). The top G6 program of 2022-25, but it keeps losing coaches: Willie Fritz to Houston (2023), Jon Sumrall to Florida (2025). MBB: Ron Hunter; no NCAA trip since 1995.

headFootballCoach.name: Will Hall
headFootballCoach.note: From memory: Sumrall left for Florida after 2025, and the Hall hire (former Tulane OC, ex-Southern Miss HC) is not verified

notes: Former SEC member (1932-66). Private AAU research university. Its 2022-25 football run makes it the American's best on-field P4 candidate, but a small fan base and stadium cap its value. Low state political pressure. Big donors (Yulman, Wilson) fund facilities. Constant coach poaching is a recurring storyline.

name: The University of Tulsa

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; believed partial cap. Amount not public.

stadium.name: Skelly Field at H.A. Chapman Stadium

athletics.note: Private school, not in the USA Today database.

ratingNotes: FB: reached the 2020 American title game. Kevin Wilson was fired in 2024, and Tre Lamb (from ETSU) has been rebuilding since 2025. MBB: a coaching cradle (Nolan Richardson, Tubby Smith, Bill Self) with a 2000 Elite Eight. Eric Konkol since 2022.

president.name: Brad R. Carson
president.title: President
president.note: Not verified; he may have departed. Check the current TU president.

notes: Smallest enrollment in FBS (~4,000). Private, with historical Presbyterian ties. Conference path: Missouri Valley, WAC, C-USA (2005), American (2014). Oil-money city philanthropy (Kaiser, Chapman) does not translate into athletics spending at P4 scale. It is the most likely odd-man-out if the American ever contracts or splits. Low state pressure.

name: University of Alabama at Birmingham

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; partial-cap payments. Amount not verified.

ratingNotes: FB: shut down in Dec 2014, restored for 2017, then won C-USA titles under Bill Clark (2018, 2020). Trent Dilfer (2023-25) was fired in Oct 2025. MBB: Andy Kennedy; 2024 American tournament champs (NCAA); a perennial upper-half team. Gene Bartow-era 1982 Elite Eight.

president.name: Ray L. Watts
president.title: President
president.note: Not verified for 2026; a succession may have occurred

headFootballCoach.name: Alex Mortensen
headFootballCoach.note: Interim after Dilfer was fired in Oct 2025. The permanent hire for 2026 was not verified, and this name may be wrong.

notes: Governed by the University of Alabama System Board of Trustees. Many in Birmingham see the board as Tuscaloosa-dominated, and it oversaw the 2014 shutdown of football. That makes system politics an event lever. The city-built Protective Stadium (2021) is a strong G6 venue. Moved C-USA to the American in 2023. Battle for the Bones rivalry with Memphis.

name: The University of Texas at San Antonio

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; partial-cap payments. Amount not verified.
athletics.note: Approximate finances. Football plays in the city-owned Alamodome.

ratingNotes: FB: football started in 2011 (FCS) and reached FBS in 2012-13. Jeff Traylor won C-USA titles in 2021 and 2022, contended in the American in 2023, and won the 2024 Myrtle Beach Bowl. 2025 was middling (record not verified). MBB: weak; Austin Claunch since 2024.
notes: UT System school that merged with UT Health San Antonio in 2025, making it larger and more research-heavy. San Antonio is the biggest US metro without a P4 program, the core of a Big 12 pitch. UT Regents and the Texas Legislature mean high political leverage. Its I-35 rival Texas State left for the Pac-12, a sore point. Red McCombs' legacy (died 2023) still shapes donor culture.

name: Wichita State University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in (no football); money goes mainly to basketball and baseball. Amount not verified.

ratingNotes: No football since 1986. MBB: 2013 Final Four and a 35-0 start in 2014 under Gregg Marshall, who resigned in 2020. Last NCAA trip 2021 (First Four). Paul Mills since 2022. Koch Arena sellouts carry the fan rating. Olympic: baseball won the 1989 CWS.
notes: The American's only non-football full member (joined 2017 from the MVC). Dropped football after the 1986 season, and the 1970 team plane crash is part of its identity. Studies of reinstating football come up periodically, a possible event. The Koch family (Koch Industries HQ in Wichita; arena naming) anchors boosters. In a football-driven split it is the most exposed member; a basketball-league landing such as the Big East or a rebuilt MVC is a possible storyline. Kansas Board of Regents oversight.
